findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the parser's two-character format
findings.body: The encoder concatenates `getShortcut()` directly into the token ID, but decoding requires the context prefix to be exactly six characters. `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not enforce a two-character value and its documentation even describes a three-letter shortcut as typical. A custom grant using a three-character shortcut will therefore issue IDs that this provider cannot decode, causing later context lookups to fail with `IllegalArgumentException`. Either enforce and document the two-character contract or make parsing support variable-length shortcuts.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies characters `[4,6)`, but this matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which overlaps the token-type prefix. It also returns `false` when that substring equals the expected shortcut. Consequently, event assertions do not detect an incorrect grant shortcut and can reject some otherwise valid IDs. Read the actual grant segment and compare it against the expected shortcut.

findings.title: The raw token ID null check validates the grant type twice
findings.body: This second `requireNonNull` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`, so a context with a null raw ID is accepted. Passing it to `encodeTokenId` then produces an ID ending in the literal `null` rather than rejecting the invalid context. Validate `rawTokenId` here.
